sections.title: Applications of differentiation to geometry problems

classification.difficultyReason: Combine product and chain rules, then use positivity for an arbitrary positive integer to exclude every horizontal tangent.

content.prompt: Let $n$ be any positive integer. Show that the curve $f(x)=x(x^2+1)^n$ has no horizontal tangent.

answer.short: $f'(x)=(x^2+1)^{n-1}[(1+2n)x^2+1]>0$ for every real $x$. Hence the curve has no horizontal tangent.

sections.title: Applications of differentiation to geometry problems

classification.difficultyReason: Derive a tangent with symbolic parameters and prove that its axis-intercept triangle has constant area.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $P\left(cp,\dfrac{c}{p}\right)$, where $c\ne0$ is a constant and $p\ne0$, lies on the hyperbola $xy=c^2$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw a sketch of the hyperbola and label any point $P$ on the curve.

answer.short: A rectangular hyperbola with branches in quadrants I and III, asymptotic to both coordinate axes, with $P\left(cp,\dfrac{c}{p}\right)$ labelled.
answer.worked: Write $y=\dfrac{c^2}{x}$. Since $c^2>0$, the branches lie in quadrants I and III. The coordinate axes are asymptotes. Label a point $P\left(cp,\dfrac{c}{p}\right)$ on either branch. The sketch shows a representative point on the positive branch.

spec.description: Authored schematic solution sketch with both hyperbola branches, coordinate axes and a representative point P. No numerical scale is asserted.
spec.mathematics: xy=c^2 with c nonzero; both axes are asymptotes. The positive-branch representative is drawn in normalized coordinates.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that the tangent at $P$ has equation $x+p^2y=2cp$. Draw the tangent on your sketch.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=\frac{c^2}{x}\\y'&=-\frac{c^2}{x^2}\\m_{\text{tangent}}&=-\frac{c^2}{(cp)^2}\\&=-\frac{1}{p^2}\end{aligned}$$
Using $P\left(cp,\dfrac{c}{p}\right)$:
$$\begin{aligned}y-\frac{c}{p}&=-\frac{1}{p^2}(x-cp)\\p^2y-cp&=-x+cp\\x+p^2y&=2cp\end{aligned}$$
Draw this line through $P$ on the sketch.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch extending part b with the tangent and its intercepts. A dashed line distinguishes the tangent from the hyperbola. Representative positive-branch configuration.
spec.mathematics: In normalized coordinates the representative curve is XY=1, P=(1,1), and its tangent X+Y=2. Symbolic intercept labels are A=(2cp,0), B=(0,2c/p).

children.label: d
children.prompt: The tangent intersects the $x$ and $y$ axes at $A$ and $B$ respectively. Show that the area of $\triangle OAB$ will always be the same, regardless of where the tangent was drawn.

answer.short: The area is always $2c^2$ square units, independent of $p$.
answer.worked:
At the $x$-intercept, $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}x&=2cp\end{aligned}$$
At the $y$-intercept, $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}p^2y&=2cp\\y&=\frac{2c}{p}\end{aligned}$$
The perpendicular side lengths are $|2cp|$ and $\left|\dfrac{2c}{p}\right|$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area of }\triangle OAB&=\frac12|2cp|\left|\frac{2c}{p}\right|\\&=2c^2\end{aligned}$$
Since $c$ is constant and the result does not depend on $p$, the area is always the same.

teachingContext.methodNote: The review revisits line intercepts, tangent and normal equations, and triangle areas using perpendicular coordinate-axis bases. The supplied solution on page 75 differentiates y=c²/x and uses point–gradient form.

The supplied blue answers show the product cp(c/p)=c², a Desmos sketch reference, derivative −c²/x², tangent gradient −1/p², equation x+p²y=2cp, intercepts 2cp and 2c/p, and constant area 2c².
